detailed_description: The Text Cleaner tool performs advanced text normalization through regex pattern matching and Unicode-aware processing. It systematically identifies and removes zero-width spaces, non-breaking spaces (U+00A0), and other invisible characters that disrupt text analysis. By leveraging PCRE2-compatible regex engines, it collapses consecutive whitespace sequences into single spaces while preserving intentional indentation through smart tab detection. Developers working with messy dataset imports or scraped web content benefit from its ability to standardize line terminators (CRLF/LF) and eliminate UTF-8 byte order marks (BOM). The tool's multistage processing pipeline first tokenizes text blocks, applies configurable transformation rules, and finally performs grapheme cluster validation to maintain emoji integrity. Use cases include preparing JSON data for schema validation, cleaning HTML output for parser compatibility, and standardizing log files prior to ELK stack ingestion. Technical features include case conversion toggles (ASCII-safe upper/lower), smart quote normalization (U+2018/U+2019), and customizable duplicate line removal with hash-based comparison.
usage_steps: Paste raw text into the input text area or drag-and-drop a .txt/.csv file
Enable 'Normalize Unicode' to resolve diacritic inconsistencies
Adjust whitespace handling using the 'Collapse Spaces' slider (1-4 space tolerance)
Select line termination mode: Unix (LF), Windows (CRLF), or Preserve Original
Toggle 'Remove Duplicates' to activate hash-based line comparison
Click 'Process Text' and download results via the progress-tracked export button
usage_examples: Cleaning Wikipedia API responses containing hidden HTML comments and inconsistent spacing
Standardizing Python script indentation after cross-platform editing issues
Preprocessing customer CSV uploads for Salesforce data import validation
Sanitizing JSON-LD test data with mixed line terminators for W3C validator compliance
